QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_10

question.text: Under Regulation 29 of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, an AIF shall be wound up if investors pass a resolution at a meeting of unit-holders. The required consent threshold is:

answer.text: Simple majority (>50%) by value of investment
Two-thirds of unit-holders by value of investment
75% of investors by value of their investment

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 29(1)(c) requires 75% of investors BY VALUE to resolve winding-up. Other triggers are tenure expiry, trustee opinion in investor interest, or SEBI direction. The same 75% threshold applies to in-specie distribution of unliquidated investments. **The Trap:** Simple majority confuses with ordinary corporate resolutions. 2/3rd is the tenure-extension threshold — a common swap. Unanimity is too high and not required anywhere in the AIF Regs. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B often ask students to distinguish 2/3rd (extension) from 75% (wind-up, material change, in-specie). XIX-C goes deeper into process: trustee intimation, no new investments, liquidation period. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When proposing early wind-up to LPs, route the resolution only after securing 75%+ soft commitments in writing. A failed wind-up vote is a signalling disaster to the secondary market and will compress any eventual GP-led CV pricing.
